title: YesSql Indexes: Query Your Own Documents

steps.text: Orchard Core stores most of its data as JSON documents, and an index is what lets you query them. In this video, you define a YesSql index, register it, create its table, and query it with ISession.

Orchard Core does not use an ORM such as Entity Framework. Content items, users, settings, and workflows are saved with YesSql, a document database interface over a relational database: SQL Server, SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL.
YesSql serializes an object to JSON and stores it as a row of a document table. There is no schema to migrate, so adding a part or a field to a content type never requires a database migration.
The limit is that SQL cannot query inside a JSON document efficiently. An index solves it: a plain class with the properties you want to query, kept by YesSql in a regular SQL table.
When a document is created, updated, or deleted, YesSql recomputes its index rows in the same transaction. A property you query must be part of an index. Everything else stays only in the JSON.

chapters.title: A map index
chapters.subtitle: From a document to index rows

steps.text: A map index is a class that inherits from MapIndex. Its properties are the columns you query on. ProductIndex has a Sku, a Price, and the Published flag of the content item.
An IndexProvider describes how to map a document type to index rows. In Describe, For names the index, When selects the content items that have a ProductPart, and Map builds a row from the part.
Each version of a content item is its own document, so ProductIndex has a row for every version. The Published flag lets a query choose the published version.
Map can return null, and the document then has no row. AliasPartIndex does this when the alias is empty. It is a map index too, with rows only for content items that have an AliasPart.

chapters.title: Register and create the table
chapters.subtitle: The provider and a data migration

steps.text: In the Startup class of your module, AddIndexProvider registers the provider as a singleton. A provider that needs scoped services implements IScopedIndexProvider, and AddScopedIndexProvider registers it at the session level.

The index table comes from a data migration. CreateMapIndexTableAsync declares a column for each property. The documentation on data migrations advises setting the length of every string column, as Sku does here.

AlterIndexTableAsync with CreateIndex adds a database index on DocumentId and the columns you filter on, which speeds up those queries. Orchard Core runs the migration when the tenant starts. A separate video covers data migrations.
Inject ISession and call Query with the document type and the index type. The predicate filters the index table with SQL, and YesSql then loads and deserializes the matching documents.

The session is a unit of work: SaveAsync and Delete are buffered, and SaveChangesAsync runs the commands in one transaction. Orchard Core calls it when the shell scope of the tenant ends. A session from any other scope is not committed for you.
To combine indexes, call With on the query. Orchard Core's user picker filters users through UserByRoleNameIndex and UserIndex, and takes 50 of the matches.
For content items, prefer IContentManager, which handles loading, versions, and handlers. Use ISession when you need to query your own indexes.
A reduce index aggregates a group of documents, like a SQL GROUP BY. UserByRoleNameIndex holds a RoleName and a Count. Map emits a row for each role of a user, and Group chooses RoleName as the key.
Reduce adds the counts of a group into one row. Delete subtracts the counts of the removed rows, and returns null when none is left. CreateReduceIndexTableAsync creates its table.
The SQL Queries feature adds Run SQL Query, under Search, Queries. It runs SQL against the database of the site, and adds the table prefix of the tenant for you.
A link on this page queries all content items. It selects every row of ContentItemIndex, the table that YesSql keeps in step with the content item documents.
Each result is a row of the index. It holds the columns of ContentItemIndex, including a DocumentId that points back to the document the row was computed from.
A reduce index row does not point to one document: it aggregates a group of them. In UserByRoleNameIndex, each row is a role, with the Count of the users that have it.
A map index can hold several records for a document. A query that joins it must then group its matches by document, and a page has to read every match before it can be sorted.
SingleRecordPerDocument declares that the map returns at most one record per document. A query that joins only such indexes is not grouped, and saving a document throws if the map returns several.

ExclusiveToDocumentType declares that only documents of the provider's type have records in the index, so a count reads the index tables without joining the document table. ContentItemIndex declares both.

NoIndexOptimizations opts a query out of these optimizations, as Orchard Core does for a text search in the content picker. SkipDeduplication skips the grouping when a query joins an index with several records but matches only one.
That's a YesSql index: a class, a provider, a table, and a query through ISession. The documentation page, How YesSql works, goes through each step. Thanks for watching.
